title: Sunrise handbook, changelog draft, and dayplan
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact operator-facing handbook for the upcoming ‘Sunrise’ feature bundle (internal name). It combines the preflight checklist, an hour-by-hour dayplan for launch, and a draft changelog/release notes skeleton intended for product review and legal scrub. Keep terse — this doc is for on-call launch operators and product owners who will be shepherding the first 72h of traffic.

Audience:
- Release engineers and operators
- Product manager (PM) owners and release leads
- On-call SREs and monitoring owners
- Solutions / SEs covering early customers

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Sunrise is a coordinated feature bundle (model routing changes + API telemetry flags + console UX updates) targeting GA rollout to hosted customers on 2026-11-10. We expect modest traffic uplift from beta customers; primary risk vectors are increased tail latency from the new routing rule and two new metrics emitters that touch the telemetry pipeline. This handbook contains preflight gates, a minute-level dayplan, a draft changelog for customer-facing notes, and rollback/mitigation playbooks.

High-level rollout dates (calendar):
- 2026-11-02: Freeze non-critical PRs for release windows (code freeze)
- 2026-11-04: Telemetry smoke run in staging (golden path internal test)
- 2026-11-06: Canary gating (1% traffic, internal + sample beta customers)
- 2026-11-08: Canary review + broaden to 10% if gating clear
- 2026-11-10 09:00 UTC: Target GA open window (gradual ramp to 100% over 6h)
- 2026-11-17: 7-day post-release retro and metrics review

Preflight checklist (must pass before 11-06 canary):
- Code & infra:
  - All PRs merged into release branch are green and have passing e2e smoke tests (PR checklist + test coverage).
  - Feature flags implemented with the correct scoping keys (user, org, region).
  - Migration scripts dry-run completed; no schema drift detected.
- Observability:
  - Dashboards for new routing metrics created and pinned in Ops board.
  - Alerts configured: latency_p99 > 750ms (prod), error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 2m.
  - Sampling for traces of the golden path enabled (1/10 for canary).
- Capacity & performance:
  - Load test with representative traffic profile (1x expected burst) completed and SLOs met.
  - Autoscaling policy reviewed for the dedicated pool and dedicated-canary quota set.
- Security & compliance:
  - Secrets reviewed and KMS rotation scheduled; no new entitlements required.
  - Data residency checks for routing rules verified against customer tags.
- Communication:
  - Slack channel #release-sunrise created and invited on-call, PM, SRE, SEs.
  - External beta customers notified about canary window with contact info for fast feedback.

Canary gating criteria (pass/fail):
- Latency: p95 within 1.15x baseline; p99 < 2x baseline and absolute p99 < 1s threshold.
- Errors: overall error rate not above 0.5% and critical error signals (auth, inference-failure) show no increasing trend.
- Business metrics: cost-per-token within expected model-variant band (±12%).
- Stability: no unhandled exceptions or increases in retry loops observed in logs for 30m.

Day-of release (2026-11-10) hour-by-hour plan (operators only):
- 07:00 UTC: Pre-shift sync (15m) — final go/no-go check from PM, SRE lead, and release engineer. Confirm all preflight items remain green.
- 08:00 UTC: Open canary to 10% traffic for broader internal beta. Monitor first 30m.
- 09:00 UTC: If canary stable, ramp to 30% over 30m. Post-ramp check-in 10:00 UTC.
- 10:00 UTC: Ramp diagnostic window: hold 15m; validate p95/p99 and telemetry throughput. If metrics drift, pause and investigate.
- 10:30 UTC: If green, ramp to 60% over 45m.
- 11:15 UTC: Hold and run customer-facing sanity checks (API smoke, OAuth flows, embed creation).
- 12:00 UTC: Final ramp to 100% over 2h. Begin 2h close monitoring window post-100%
- 14:30 UTC: If no major regressions, begin sampling expansion to 1/5 traces for live traffic for debugging.
- 16:00 UTC: Release lead posts preliminary release note stub to #release-sunrise and notifies stakeholder list.
- 20:00 UTC: Nightshift handoff notes prepared if any issues — otherwise prepare 24h passive monitoring cadence.

Draft changelog / release notes (customer-facing draft — keep short):
Title: Sunrise Feature Bundle — Nov 10, 2026 (beta -> GA)
Highlights:
- Smarter model routing: requests now route to optimized model variants by latency profile, reducing median latency for short prompts by ~12% in internal benchmarks.
- Enhanced telemetry for inference flows: richer event details for traceability and cost analytics (opt-in for Private deployments).
- Console UX improvements: new route visualization and per-route cost breakdown for multi-model routes.

Detailed (for release notes page):
- Model routing policy: Introduces a new policy engine that selects model variants based on prompt length and user tier. Default behavior preserves prior model assignment for existing customers; opt-in is controlled by feature flag.
- Telemetry schema: added fields route_id, model_variant_hint, and inference_cost_estimate to the inference event. Customers using strict schema filters should plan for ingestion updates.
- Console: added per-route latency heatmap and token-cost trend charts.

Known issues (work in progress):
- Edge case: Rare race where KV cache warmup can cause transient p99 spikes during high-concurrency bursts. Mitigation in place (throttle warmup) but telemetry still collecting incidence rates.
- Migration note: Customers with strict downstream parsing rules may need to update ingestion mapping to accept the new telemetry fields.

Post-release validation & telemetry checks (first 72h):
- Continuous: monitor latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, and cost-per-token daily.
- Day 0–1: watch for error spike patterns and new exception signatures; page SRE if p99 > 1s sustained for 10m.
- Day 1–3: run sample replay of golden path traces to ensure quality parity; compare model outputs on a fixed prompt set.
- Day 7: scheduled metrics review and gating to mark this release as stable for business reporting.

Rollback criteria and quick steps:
Criteria to trigger rollback:
- Sustained p99 > 1.5s for 10 minutes and manual investigation identifies routing change as primary cause.
- Error rate > 1% for 5m with root cause traced to new telemetry layer causing downstream backpressure.
- Critical customer impact reported with validated reproducible rollback test.
Quick rollback steps (operator):
1) Switch feature flag: revert routing policy to ‘legacy’ mode (feature-flag toggle).
2) If flag fails, revert the routing service deploy-version to previous release via release orchestration UI (blue/green fallback).
3) Engage SRE pager and open incident in JIRA (JIRA-RUNBOOK template).

Communication templates (short):
- Slack (internal): "@channel Sunrise GA opened to 100% at 2026-11-10 12:00 UTC. Monitoring now; ping @oncall-SRE for anomalies. Release notes draft posted: <link>"
- Customer email (beta customers pre-canary): "We will route a small portion of traffic to the new routing policy between 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-10. Expect no downtime; please report regressions to support@redwood.ai with subject 'Sunrise canary'."

Action items (owners):
- Maya Chen: publish final changelog to docs site and coordinate legal skim (by 2026-11-09 18:00 UTC).
- Diego Torres: run final load test and confirm autoscale thresholds (by 2026-11-05 EOD).
- Asha Raman: pin dashboards and configure paging rules (by 2026-11-05 EOD).
- PM (Elena Vaz): confirm customer communication list and sign-off (by 2026-11-06 morning).

Open questions / risks:
- How will multi-region routing behave under asymmetric regional load? Need a chaos run for region-failover scenario.
- Do enterprise customers require a rollout holdback window for control-plane-only changes?
- Are HSM/KMS rotations risk-free during the window? Ops to validate with security.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Staging smoke checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Staging+Smoke
- Canary go/no-go notes (workspace): https://docs.google.com/document/d/placeholder
- Incident runbook template: JIRA-RUNBOOK

Notes to self (operator scratch):
- Keep this doc short. Move longer postmortem to the release-retro page. Capture timestamps of any anomaly — exact epoch times are helpful for correlating traces.

End.
